transcript.text: Alright everyone, before we finalize the design for the new event-ingestion service, I want to make sure we go through our standard sign-off checklist. We've got the draft design on the table — active-active replication, 90-day event-retention period, and 96 partitions to start. The prototype already passed functional tests across both US and EU tenants, which is good. But since we're targeting production next Monday, I need to hear from each area: backend engineering, infrastructure, customer success operations, and security — any blockers or required controls from your side before I record the final design?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While reviewing an unrelated consumer integration this morning, I confirmed that the existing Ledger event consumer cannot preserve ordering across active-active replication. Production compatibility requires active-passive replication plus an explicit per-aggregate ordering guardrail. I have not yet updated the architecture document.

transcript.text: I need to flag a blocker from infrastructure. I confirmed from the current production load model ten minutes ago that the shared cluster can only support 48 partitions for this service without starving the checkout stream — not the 96 in the draft. I was still reconciling the capacity worksheet and hadn't posted the number yet, but given we're finalizing now, everyone needs to know.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a blocker from customer success operations. In a contract review this afternoon, I found that the enterprise tenant Linden requires all event processing and storage to remain in the EU region — no cross-region replication permitted. Linden is included in the proposed initial cohort, and I have not yet added a routing exception to the design ticket. This directly conflicts with the active-active replication proposal, at least for this tenant.
